before.descent: Descend the Southwest Couloir (standard route) toward the approach side.

itinerary.cal: Same NPS backcountry permit zone; a committing IV+ 5.10 outing best attempted mid-July through September when the glacier/moat is most passable and rock is driest.

days.note: PCT south from Bridge Creek trailhead, up North Fork Bridge Creek, then a brushy, off-trail approach (the first-ascent party logged roughly 3,000 ft of bushwhacking) to a camp near the Goode Glacier below the ridge's start.
days.title: Approach to high camp/bivy
days.objective: Reach a bivy below the ridge

days.note: A long, sustained alpine rock climb along the crest with 4,000-5,000 ft of exposure on either side; simul-climbing up to 5.8 with harder pitches (up to 5.10) higher on the ridge. The first-ascent party spent about 11-12 hours climbing before bivying on the summit, the highest point in North Cascades National Park.
days.title: Climb Megalodon Ridge to a summit bivy

schedule.label: Leave bivy
schedule.detail: Approach the base of the ridge across the glacier.

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: Simul-climb easier 4th/low-5th terrain on the lower ridge.

schedule.label: Crux pitches
schedule.detail: Sustained 5.8-5.10 crack and stemming moves on the ridge crest.

schedule.label: Upper ridge
schedule.detail: Continued exposed climbing; route eases somewhat near the top.

days.objective: Climb the full ridge to the summit

days.note: Descend the standard Southwest Couloir descent line, then keep losing elevation toward the Bridge Creek drainage rather than returning to the Day 1 camp. Expect several rappels and tired legs after the previous day's long climb.
days.title: Descend toward Bridge Creek
days.objective: Rappel/downclimb the Southwest Couloir toward the valley

days.note: Finish down North Fork Bridge Creek and the PCT back to Highway 20.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Bridge Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A serious 4-day, grade IV+ 5.10 alpine outing: a brushy approach, an 11-12 hour technical ridge climb to a summit bivy, then a long multi-day descent and hike-out via the Southwest Couloir — roughly 35 mi and 7,500 ft of gain round trip.

weather.typical: Cold North Cascades alpine; afternoon clouds and showers common
weather.probability: Afternoon clouds/showers can turn a long ridge day into a forced, unplanned bivy

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Extreme - sustained, highly exposed climbing over many towers deep in NCNP; a fall, injury, or delay on the ridge creates serious benightment and rescue risk on a very long route

avalanche.zone: N/A - non-glaciated summer rock ridge route

seasonal_hazards.crevasses: N/A - no glacier travel is documented for this ridge route; approach details near any glaciated terrain are not fully verified

before.approach: Follow Thunder Creek Trail from Colonial Creek Campground (SR-20 MP130) about 9 miles to the Fisher Creek Trail junction, then Fisher Creek Trail about 3 miles to a lake camp near 5,160 ft below the Banded Glacier.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the PCT North trailhead parking at Rainy Pass on SR-20 (~4,860 ft)

itinerary.cal: Easy Pass Trail typically isn't snow-free until July. Highway 20 access to the Easy Pass Trailhead is seasonal — typically open mid-April/May through early December, but exact dates vary by year and by winter storm damage (confirm via WSDOT); the trailhead sits inside the MP134-171 winter closure zone. The longer Thunder Creek Trailhead alternate is open year-round if Easy Pass is still gated. An NPS backcountry permit is required for the lake camp.

days.note: Hike the Easy Pass Trail up and over the pass (~6,600 ft), descend into the Fisher Creek drainage, then leave trail to reach a basin lake camp near the toe of the Banded Glacier — expect a sketchy log-bridge creek crossing and boggy ground near the lake.
days.title: Approach to Banded Glacier basin camp
days.objective: Reach the lake camp below the Banded Glacier

days.note: A long alpine day: climb loose talus and a rockfall-prone gully to the obscure, hard-to-spot Christmas Tree Col, drop into the Banded Glacier basin, rope up and stay climber's-left of the crevasses to the Banded-Douglas col, then follow a loose Class 2-3 ridge to the summit before reversing the entire route.
days.title: Summit via Christmas Tree Col and the Banded Glacier

schedule.label: Reach Christmas Tree Col
schedule.detail: Not obvious from the lake — look for an orange-brown notch above the snowfields.

schedule.label: Rope up on the Banded Glacier
schedule.detail: Stay climber's-left to avoid the worst crevasses.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Via the Banded-Douglas col and NE ridge.

days.objective: Reach the true summit and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the approach over Easy Pass back to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Easy Pass Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A strenuous 3-day, ~29-mile round trip (~12,500 ft gain) via Easy Pass; the crux is a very long (12+ hr) summit day through the loose, hard-to-find Christmas Tree Col and a roped glacier crossing. Very strong parties have linked the whole route car-to-car in a single ~13.5 hr day, but that is an outlier push, not the standard plan.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong multi-day backpacking fitness for the same long, remote Thunder Creek / Park Creek Pass approach used by the other Logan routes
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Heavy overnight glacier-mountaineering pack, plus any additional ice tools/protection for the steeper sections, roughly 35-45+ lbs

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long approach (multi-day), same remote North Cascades approach as the Banded Glacier route
requiredSkills: comfort with a long, committing, remote approach
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Advanced alpine climber — beyond general glacier-mountaineering competence, partners need comfort on steeper ice/snow steps, consistent with the harder character versus the standard routes
